To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the local thermal sensation and comfort of individual body part can be predicted from whole-body thermal sensation and comfort, and local skin temperature.

the thermal comfort of individual body-part is determined by the local sensation, which is in turn determined by the local skin and core temperatures and the whole-body sensation, which is determined by the skin temperature.
1. The local comfort model is the first to predict the local thermal comfort of individual body-part regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
predicting the thermal comfort responses to the environment of individual body parts and the whole body.
the development of thermal comfort models that apply to transient and non-uniform environments.
the development of models to predict local comfort and sensation from thermophysiological inputs, and to predict whole-body comfort and sensation from local inputs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the models in Parts I, II, and III are useful for estimating local thermal sensation and comfort responses of the human body to non-uniform transient environments.
the model presented in Part II is a significant improvement over the model of Gagge, Gonzalez, and Saltzman (1967) and the model of ASHRAE Standard 55 (2010).
the models presented here provide a basis for predicting the thermal sensation and comfort of individuals in a wide range of environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the models presented in this series are useful in predicting thermal comfort and sensation responses for a range of environments and activities.
the local comfort model for the individual parts of the human torso and limbs can be used to predict the local sensation and comfort of the individual parts.
the models are able to predict local and whole-body sensations and local and whole-body comfort with an accuracy that is similar to or better than that obtained by other methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the thermal sensations of individual parts of the body are not necessarily the same as the thermal sensations of the whole body, even when the local and whole-body temperatures and the thermal environment are the same.
the local thermal comfort of a body part depends on the local and whole-body sensations of that part, and on the local and global thermal environments.
a local thermal sensation model can be combined with a local thermal comfort model to obtain local thermal comfort responses for individual body parts.
